ORAL ORDER

The petitioner is before this Court calling in question the registration of a crime in Crime No.20/2024 registered for offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504 read with Section 34 of the IPC, under Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 and under Sections 4 of the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019.

2. Heard Sri. S.N. Sameer, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, Sri. Rangaswamy R.,
learned HCGP appearing for respondent No.1, Sri. Nizam Abbas, learned NC: 2024:KHC:44557 counsel appearing for respondent No.2 and have perused the material on record.
3.
During the pendency of these proceedings, it transpires that the parties to the lis have entered into a settlement and have placed on record such settlement along with the joint affidavit.

Terms of settlement reads as follows:
"JOINT AFFIDAVIT We, 1) Mr Farhan F, S/o M. H. Fazlulla @ Fazalulla, Aged about 38 years, R/o No.4/143-1, Bypass road, Infront of Police Ground, Kushalnagar,
Kodagu-571234,
2) Farhana Sultana W/o Farhan F, aged about 25 years, R/o No.77, Nishad Mansion,
Royal Enclave, 1st cross, Naidu Nagara, Mysuru-570 007, do hereby solemnly make oath and affirm as follows;
1) We submit that, the petitioner has preferred this petition to quash the First Information Report registered against petitioner-accused no.1 in Mysuru City Mr. Farhan F vs State By Mysuru City Women P.S on 5 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113778436/
2 Women Police Station in Crime No.20/2024 for the alleged offence punishable under Section 498 (A), 323, 504 R/w 34 and Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act 1961 and Section 4 of The Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 on the file of Hon'ble 7th Addl Civil Judge (Sr.Dn) & JMFC Court, JLB Road, Mysuru.
2) We submit that, at the instance of elders and well- wishers the petitioner and respondent No.2-informant have amicably settled all their claims,
differences, litigations and disputes against each other.
3) We submit that, the petitioner is husband of respondent No.2 and due to extreme differences between the petitioner and respondent no.2 they have resolved that the continuation of marriage would not be beneficial to both but detrimental to each other's interest and NC: 2024:KHC:44557 hence, the marriage is ended by entering into "KHULA NAMA and settlement deed".
